title: Audit Orbit: Sealed Evidence Broker for Admin Activity with Residency & Retention Controls
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a sealed evidence broker that captures admin actions, access events, and configuration changes; enforces tenant and region residency tags; stores tamper-evident snapshots in WORM-backed storage; and automates periodic notarization and exports for eDiscovery and compliance audits.
acceptance_criteria: All admin action events contain canonical residency and tenant metadata before write
Daily and on-demand evidence bundles can be produced per-tenant and per-region in signed, WORM-ready format
Stored artifacts are immutable (WORM) for retention period and include cryptographic anchors and HSM timestamps
Retention policy enforcement runs automatically and flags exceptions to compliance queue
Audit Console can stream read-only proofs (hashes/anchors) and export P7M-compatible evidence bundles
implementation_notes: Use prefix-based routing to ensure region-bound events are written to the correct WORM bucket or on-prem vault
Event pipeline: matcher -> normalizer -> WORM-prep generator -> notarizer -> sink
Notarizer: compute Merkle root over daily manifest; submit hash to HSM for timestamp/signature; persist proof alongside WORM object metadata
Retention metadata stored as immutable index entries with soft-delete markers that trigger legal-hold bypass
Design storage layout to support chunked uploads and multipart verification to satisfy large eDiscovery exports
progress_updates: 2025-03-04: Kickoff and spec draft. Identified primary stakeholders: Legal, Security, Console PM.
2025-03-07: Prototype Merkle root builder and validation harness. Initial perf target: 5M events/day per region.
2025-03-11: Integration spike with existing admin-audit stream; discovered missing tenant residency in 2.3% of events — created normalization rule
2025-03-14: HSM vendor evaluation: AWS CloudHSM vs. Azure Key Vault HSM. Chose vendor-agnostic HSM adapter to support Private deployments.
2025-03-18: First end-to-end test: manifest generation + HSM stamp + WORM write succeeded for small bundle; found timeout edge-case in multipart verification (ticketed).
decisions: Persist primary evidence objects in S3-compatible WORM buckets for Hosted and Dedicated; use on-prem vault adapter with HSM stamping for Private installs
Cryptographic anchoring via Merkle roots + HSM timestamping; optional public anchoring (blockchain) flagged as future work
Expose read-only proof endpoints in Console with RBAC to avoid accidental evidence export by non-compliance roles
tradeoffs: WORM storage provides tamper-resistance but increases eDiscovery export complexity and storage costs — mitigated by chunked exports and compressed manifests
HSM stamping adds operational complexity in Private deployments; chosen adapter pattern reduces coupling but requires customer KMS onboarding
Stricter residency enforcement can increase write latency for cross-region admin consoles — opted for synchronous residency validation with async fallback and audit event for delayed routing
testing_plan: Unit tests for Merkle builder, HSM adapter, and manifest schema
Integration test: simulated admin stream -> broker -> WORM sink with end-to-end proof validation
Performance test: ingest 6M events/day into a single region while maintaining notarization SLA
Chaos test: simulate partial WORM sink failures and validate retry semantics and duplicate suppression
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal compliance team only, Hosted staging region
Phase 2: Select pilot customers on Dedicated; enable read-only Console proofs
Phase 3: Default on for all Hosted; opt-in for Private with customer KMS configuration
Fallback: if notarizer latency > SLO, route to degraded mode and generate alert with explicit evidence footnote
audit_evidence_spec: Evidence bundle format: newline-delimited JSON events + daily manifest (manifest.json) containing event file checksums, Merkle root, HSM signature, region and residency tags. Bundle packaging: tar.gz along with detached proof files (.sig) and a human-readable attest.txt for auditors.
retention_policy_matrix: System admins (global): 7 years in home region
Support agents (cross-region): 3 years with residency-tagged replica in originating region
Configuration changes: 10 years or legal-hold override
Access tokens and ephemeral secrets: 90 days and redaction in evidence exports
final_notes: Next immediate steps: finish multipart verification fix, complete HSM adapter hardening, and schedule joint review with Legal and Security on 2025-03-25. Ensure Confluence spec includes eDiscovery sample bundle.
